usage:
Save as clean_workbook.py after operator review. Requires Python 3.10+ and openpyxl 3.1+. Run: python clean_workbook.py < input.json > output.json. Alternatively call clean_workbook(payload). Input follows the supplied schema; output contains workbook_b64. No network or spreadsheet application is used. Source has not been executed.

Processes all populated Data records, enforcing row_bound as their maximum count. Duplicate detection precedes numeric validation; an invalid first occurrence still suppresses later duplicates. IDs retain their original XML text and type. Blank numbers become zero; malformed numbers, booleans, errors and numeric formulas cause their rows to be discarded. Dates accept Excel serials, native dates, ISO text and common slash/dash formats; ambiguous dates use month-first parsing. Blank dates remain blank; unrecognized dates raise an error.

Writes actual numeric caches for every generated Amount formula and the Summary total. Other sheet XML, values and existing formula caches remain unchanged, except Summary A1/B1. This is not a general Excel formula engine: unrelated formulas are not recalculated. Macro or external-link inputs are rejected. Intended for the supplied plain Data table layout; complex tables, merged data rows and dependent formulas outside the generated columns require additional handling.
